integration.reason: The fork has a different Template V2 Studio and export architecture. Content-level ports preserve local authored, Windows, security, and export-fidelity contracts while adopting the upstream behavior.

slices.evidence: TemplateV2Canvas and TemplateV2CanvasGuides already provide alignment guides and snapping through the fork snapping library; the parallel upstream Konva implementation was not duplicated.

Pinned Chart.js, DataLabels, and Tailwind browser assets and licenses are served locally by FastAPI and Next.js. The fork collision-aware data-label renderer remains active while the upstream DataLabels runtime contract is loaded and registered.

Math is supported by the strict FastAPI discriminator and generated-content schema, hydration, Studio import/edit/render, JSON-to-HTML export, and the fork general PDF/PPTX renderer with bounded LaTeX and fail-closed KaTeX rendering.
The upstream categorized shape presets and tests are retained, while insertion dispatches through the fork generic Studio add-element history and autosave action.
Preview starts automatically after the selected file reaches the font-check step and no unavailable fonts remain, with a per-file guard and the existing manual preview path preserved.

The fork already has slideScrollSync overflow navigation and review-selection reset coverage. Thumbnail cards now add button semantics, current-slide state, focusability, and Enter/Space activation without replacing local scroll synchronization.

The local Korean dashboard now exposes a blank-presentation action with duplicate-request suppression, loading state, analytics, failure notification, and navigation to the standard presentation editor.
